rounds.fact: Yelp started in 2004 as an email-based referral service before pivoting to the review-website format it's known for today, after users kept asking for a public place to post reviews.
Yahoo Finance became one of the most-used sources for free stock quotes on the early web, at a time when real-time market data elsewhere often required a paid subscription.
Firefox launched in 2004 as a leaner alternative to a bloated Netscape, and its 'Download Day' campaign set a Guinness World Record for most software downloads in 24 hours.
Encyclopedia Britannica put its entire encyclopedia online for free in 1999, a bold bet that ad revenue could replace its centuries-old subscription business, before pulling back a year later.
CNN.com's early design crammed dozens of headlines onto one dense page, a layout style that dominated news sites for years before cleaner, story-focused redesigns took over.
